# Tomer Yona

> Personal site of Tomer Yona, PhD: wearable sensor measurement, validation and evidence generation. Also home to free tools he made, including Cuewand, a phone remote for PowerPoint.

## Cuewand: free phone remote for PowerPoint

Cuewand turns a phone into a remote control for Microsoft PowerPoint on a Windows laptop. The phone needs no app: it scans a QR code shown on the laptop (or opens a short address and types a 6-digit number) and the remote opens as a web page in the phone's browser. It is built for iPhone and Android browsers.

What the phone does:
- Next and Back (slide clicker / presentation clicker / wireless presenter replacement)
- Speaker notes on the phone, split at each animation step when the notes contain [click]; pictures of the current and next slide
- A countdown for the talk on the Next button, with on-screen alerts; on Android it also vibrates (iPhones do not let web pages vibrate)
- Laser pointer: holding the slide picture moves PowerPoint's red laser dot on the big screen
- Find a slide by title, slide text, notes or number and jump to it; after a jump to a hidden backup slide, Back returns to where you were
- Black out the screen
- Rehearsal timing, then "ahead / behind" pacing during the talk
- Any number of phones; by default every one can press Next, and control can be passed to one co-presenter while the others follow
- Works alongside a hardware clicker or the keyboard
- Tablet presenter view in landscape; left-handed layout

Requirements and limits:
- 64-bit Windows laptop with the PowerPoint desktop app, run on the computer that shows the slides and set up before the talk (not meant for an unfamiliar lectern PC). No Mac version; Keynote and PowerPoint on the web are not supported. The Windows download bundles its own Python.
- Phone and laptop connect over the same Wi-Fi, the phone's own hotspot, or an optional internet link relayed encrypted through Cloudflare quick tunnels. Same Wi-Fi traffic is not encrypted.
- Without a PowerPoint deck open, Next and Back press the laptop's arrow keys, which works for Google Slides or a full-screen PDF (no notes, slide pictures or pace; the clock still runs).
- Anyone with the pairing code or 6-digit number can control the slides while Cuewand runs; codes last twelve hours, and Make new codes on the pairing page cancels them sooner.

Testing status (version 2.3): earlier versions ran on real PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 with one presenter. Later changes were checked against a PowerPoint simulator with 598 automated checks and an automated accessibility audit. Not yet tried: any iPhone, a real Android phone since version 1.6, vibration on a real phone, the hotspot route, the internet link since a reported failure, [click] notes and sections on a real deck, PowerPoint Presenter View with two screens, and a real screen reader. The version 2.2 changes to how presses are timed are not yet confirmed on real PowerPoint.

Price and licence: free, open source (MIT). No accounts, ads, analytics or tracking; nothing is sent to the author.

- [Cuewand page, with a live interactive demo](https://www.tomeryona.com/cuewand/)
- [Source code and full manual on GitHub](https://github.com/TomerIL/cuewand)
- [Download for Windows (Cuewand-for-Windows.zip)](https://github.com/TomerIL/cuewand/releases/latest)

## Other tools

- [MVNX Viewer](https://www.tomeryona.com/mvnx-viewer/): free browser-based viewer for .mvnx motion-capture files (Movella / Xsens MVN export): 3D skeleton playback, joint-angle charts, foot contacts, centre of mass. Files are not uploaded.

## Open data

- [COMPWALK-ACL dataset on Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15624356): multi-pace IMU gait kinematics (Xsens Awinda) from 92 participants: healthy adults, healthy adolescents, and people with an ACL injury before and three months after reconstruction. CC BY 4.0. Trials are .mvnx files with paired .xlsx spreadsheets.
- [The COMPWALK-ACL paper, Scientific Data (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-06307-8): Yona T, Peskin B, Fischer A.

## About

- [Home](https://www.tomeryona.com/): postdoctoral researcher at Maastricht University; PhD in Biomedical Engineering (Technion); licensed physiotherapist. Work spans IMU, EMG, PPG and accelerometry, from single-patient assessments to 10,000-participant cohorts.
